core_thesis.thesis: A system is defined by elements, interconnections, and a function or purpose; its recurring behavior emerges largely from its structure. Sound intervention therefore begins with behavior over time, stocks, flows, feedback, delays, boundaries, information, and purpose—not isolated events or a list of parts.
core_thesis.systems_thinking_vs_linear_event_thinkin: Event-level explanations react to the latest occurrence. Systems thinking asks what pattern has persisted, what structure generates it, and how that structure may change under different conditions.
core_thesis.purpose_inferred_from_behavior: Stated goals are evidence, but the more reliable clue to a system’s operative purpose is what its sustained behavior accomplishes.
core_thesis.feedback_importance: Balancing loops seek conditions or goals; reinforcing loops amplify change. Their relative strength and changing dominance create much of a system’s behavior.
core_thesis.delay_importance: Stocks, physical processes, information, perception, and response all take time. Delays can make effective action look ineffective, invite overcorrection, or produce oscillation.
core_thesis.structure_drives_behavior: Different systems with similar feedback structure can produce similar behavior even when their visible elements differ.
core_thesis.elements_are_often_low_leverage: Replacing parts or adjusting parameters may matter, but it often leaves interconnections, rules, goals, and paradigms intact.
core_thesis.leverage_is_ranked_not_generic: Interventions differ greatly in power. Parameters are usually low leverage; information, rules, self-organization, goals, and paradigms can alter deeper structure.
core_thesis.humility_in_intervention: Models are necessarily incomplete. Intervene experimentally, disclose assumptions, watch actual behavior, learn from error, and remain prepared to revise the model.

terminology_registry.name: system
terminology_registry.summary: An interconnected set of elements organized so that it produces a function or purpose.
terminology_registry.system_problem_addressed: Prevents ambiguity or category errors involving system.
terminology_registry.system_structure: The term identifies a specific part or behavior of system structure: system.
terminology_registry.behavior_over_time: Meaning becomes visible through repeated behavior, accumulation, or response rather than a single event.
what_it_explains: An interconnected set of elements organized so that it produces a function or purpose.
what_it_does_not_explain: It does not by itself diagnose a current real-world system.
evidence_needed: Observed behavior over time and a stated system boundary when applying the term.
diagnostic_questions: What direct evidence shows that system is present in this system?
intervention_implications: Use the distinction before selecting an intervention.
misuse_warnings: Do not use “system” as a vague synonym or blame label.
